themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree AI infrastructure and hardware spending is enormous and a dominant market driver, but they split on durability, with most seeing robust demand while Goldman warns the hardware trade is over-earning, highly cyclical, and starting to roll over.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure and capex spending is booming and is a dominant driver of markets and earnings.
evidence_quotes: making AI capex the dominant driver
CIO remains constructive on the wider AI value chain
Broadcom reported robust 2Q26 results, driven by “insatiable demand” for custom AI platforms.
AI is becoming a broader supply-chain theme, not just a chip or data center theme.

facts_contested.claim: Whether AI hardware/capex demand is durable or structurally over-earning and about to roll over
facts_contested.for_evidence: we don’t buy into that, particularly as the narrative of excessive funding needs doesn’t stack up
facts_contested.against_evidence: I still think AI hardware is structurally over earning and highly cyclical.

themes.consensus_view: Most desks and wires flag the Strait of Hormuz as a live oil-and-shipping risk to monitor, but only Rabobank calls for escalation while others frame it as normalizing or just a price premium, so there is no shared directional view.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks and wire sources reference the Strait of Hormuz as a live risk to oil supply and shipping that they are actively monitoring.

facts_contested.claim: Whether the Strait of Hormuz situation is normalizing or escalating
facts_contested.against_evidence: the ‘Battle of Hormuz’ may be about to begin.

themes.consensus_view: Only HSBC stakes a firm call, expecting the Fed to hold interest rates in the 3.50-3.75% range through 2027, while five other desks merely flag upcoming Fed meetings and minutes as a catalyst without committing to a direction, some noting a risk the Fed turns hawkish and raises rates.

facts_agreed.claim: HSBC expects the Fed to keep the federal funds target rate on hold through 2026-27.
evidence_quotes: Our own long-held forecast is that the FOMC will keep the federal funds target range

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag upcoming FOMC meetings and minutes as a near-term rates catalyst this window.

themes.consensus_view: Five banks flag the US-Iran conflict as a live geopolitical driver of oil prices, but they split between escalation and de-escalation framings and none has staked a firm directional call.

facts_agreed.claim: Five banks reference the US-Iran conflict as an active geopolitical catalyst this window, mainly as a driver of oil-price moves.

themes.consensus_view: Most banks treat memory chips and semiconductors as the market's dominant theme with supply staying tight and profits surging, but at least one desk warns the rally looks technically stretched and could reverse sharply.

facts_agreed.claim: Semiconductors and memory chips are the leading equity theme, backed by supply that stays tight.
evidence_quotes: Memory/Semis continue to be the dominant equity theme
We see semiconductor wafers in tight supply for the foreseeable future

facts_contested.claim: near-term direction of the semiconductor sector
facts_contested.for_evidence: We see semiconductor wafers in tight supply for the foreseeable future
facts_contested.against_evidence: Semis look to be playing out a very similar path to silver

themes.consensus_view: Four bank desks flag a US-Iran peace deal as a live macro backdrop, but none has staked a directional market view on it yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks reference a US-Iran diplomatic resolution as a contextual macro development this window.

themes.consensus_view: Three research desks reference Kevin Warsh as the Federal Reserve Chair and flag a potential shift toward tighter interest-rate policy, but none has committed to a directional call on what he will actually do.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve Chair and note his tenure as a live macro backdrop, with some framing a possible move toward tighter policy.
evidence_quotes: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh policy panel in Sintra
Kevin Warsh hawkish Fed policy shift
